name: MeetingHub – Appointment Booking Calendar & Meetings with Zoom, Google Meet, Teams, Webex & Jitsi
author: Sovlix

sections.description:
MeetingHub is a free appointment booking and scheduling plugin for WordPress that gives every booking its own Zoom, Google Meet, Microsoft Teams, Webex or Jitsi meeting link.

Share a booking page, and clients pick a time from your real availability, on their own clock. The booking is confirmed at once, both of you get an email with a calendar file, and the join link is already in it.

Many booking plugins sell video conferencing as a paid extra. MeetingHub includes all five video platforms in the free plugin, with no cap on booking pages, appointments or meetings, no commission, and every client record kept in your own WordPress database. The same plugin also creates and lists your Zoom meetings and webinars, Google Meet, Teams, Webex and Jitsi meetings.

🔥 Get MeetingHub PRO | 📖 Docs | 🤝 Join Community | 🕹️ YouTube

🏆 Why MeetingHub

  • Video on every booking, free: Zoom, Google Meet, Microsoft Teams, Webex and Jitsi Meet are all in the free plugin, and each page picks its own.
  • Works before you connect anything: Jitsi Meet needs no account, so your first booking can have a working meeting link in two minutes.
  • No limits, no commission: unlimited booking pages, appointments and meetings, with nothing taken from what you charge.
  • Your clients stay yours: names, emails and bookings live in your WordPress database, ready to export or erase.
  • Made for WordPress: blocks, Elementor, shortcodes, Yoast SEO and Rank Math sitemaps, multisite and translations.

✅ Appointment Booking Calendar

Set your hours once, share a link, and people book the times you have free.

  • A booking page for every service: each one has its own address, such as /booking/consultation/, with a month view and the free times of the chosen day.
  • Your booking calendar anywhere: paste [meetinghub_booking link="your-link"], add the Booking page block, or open it in a popup from any button or menu link.
  • Weekly hours and days off: working hours per day, days off, and different hours on a single date. New pages follow your site defaults.
  • Buffers, notice and booking window: gaps around each appointment, a minimum notice, how far ahead people may book, and how often start times appear.
  • Time zones handled: visitors see every time on their own clock and can switch zones. Your hours stay on yours.
  • No double bookings: each slot is claimed in the database, so two people clicking the same time cannot both get it.
  • Video, phone, in person or your own link: every page picks one way to meet.
  • A short booking form: name, email, a phone field with the country code, and notes. Custom questions (Pro).
  • Clients reschedule or cancel themselves: every confirmation carries a private link, and a client can say why they cancel.
  • Your own thank-you message: tell clients what happens next the moment they book.
  • Hidden booking pages: bookable by their link, left out of every list.
  • Ready from the start: your first booking page is made for you, and new ones start from a use case such as Consultation, Discovery call or Tutoring session.
  • Import from Calendly: bring your event types over as booking pages, with their link names and your working hours.
  • Bookable by AI assistants: on WordPress 6.9 or later, an AI assistant connected to your site can find your free times and book them.
  • Team booking pages (Pro): round robin or all hosts together, and hosts who are not administrators.
  • Routing forms (Pro): ask a question or two, then send each visitor to the right page.
  • Group and recurring bookings (Pro): several places per time, and the same slot every week or two.
  • Approval, limits and holidays (Pro): confirm each booking yourself, cap bookings a day or a week, save schedules, and close every calendar for a holiday.
  • Protected booking pages (Pro): a password, single-use links, or work email only.

✅ Payments for Appointments (Pro)

  • Card payments (Pro): clients pay by card, Apple Pay or Google Pay on Stripe before the booking is confirmed, with refunds in one click.
  • Deposits, extras, tax and tips (Pro): charge part up front, sell add-ons at checkout, and add a tax line or a tip.
  • Session packages (Pro): sell 5 or 10 sessions at once, booked later with a code.

✅ Video Meetings on Zoom, Google Meet, Teams, Webex and Jitsi

Each meeting and each booking page picks its own platform, so one site can run all five.

  • Zoom: meetings and webinars, host and alternative hosts, auto recording, and Join in browser so guests need no Zoom app.
  • Google Meet: every meeting is a real Google Calendar event, with its attendees and time zone.
  • Microsoft Teams: meetings over a secure Microsoft Graph connection, with lobby settings.
  • Webex: meetings with breakout sessions, meeting lock, auto recording and join before host.
  • Jitsi Meet: no account needed, on a public server, your own domain or 8×8 JaaS.
  • Meeting setup: defaults for every platform on one screen, with a preview of what guests see, and a step-by-step connection guide for each.
  • Meeting pages: a countdown, a Join button, and your choice of header, footer and sidebar. More themes, layouts, an agenda and Add to calendar (Pro).
  • Show meetings anywhere: the MeetingHub Event block and Elementor widget show a meeting as a card, a compact card or its full page.
  • Members-only meetings: limit a meeting to buyers of a WooCommerce product or BricksMembers members, and a meeting list to chosen roles or users.
  • My Meetings: [mhub-my-meetings] shows a signed-in member their upcoming sessions and bookings, each with a Join button.
  • Registration, recurring meetings, recordings and reports (Pro): on the platforms that support them.
  • Front-end meetings (Pro): members create and manage their own meetings from the front of your site.
  • Courses and marketplaces (Pro): Tutor LMS, LearnPress, LifterLMS and Academy LMS courses; Dokan, WCFM and MultiVendorX vendors; meetings sold with WooCommerce.

✅ Booking Page Themes, SEO and Languages

  • Classic theme in Light and Dark: set once for every booking page on Booking setup → Page design, previewed on your own page.
  • 18 designer themes (Pro): Summit, Sage, Calm and more, plus the Waves, Aura and Botanica styles, in any colour, with a theme per page and Match my brand.
  • Search and sharing: give each booking page its own search title, description and share image. Pages you show in search join your sitemap, including Yoast SEO and Rank Math.
  • In your visitor’s language: add ?lang= and a language code to a page link to open it in that language.
  • QR code for every page (Pro).

✅ Booking Emails, Reminders and Calendar Files

  • Eight booking emails: confirmation, reminder, rescheduled and cancelled for the client; new, moved, cancelled and no meeting link for you. Each one can be edited, previewed, tested or switched off.
  • Appointment reminder email: one before each appointment, from one hour to one week ahead.
  • Calendar file on every confirmation: an .ics attachment that adds the appointment to Google Calendar, Outlook or Apple Calendar.
  • Know your emails arrived: a log of every booking email, failures first, with a Send again button.
  • Text messages (Pro): confirmations and reminders from your own Twilio number.
  • More emails and automations (Pro): follow-ups, no-show notes, extra reminders and webhooks to Zapier, Make or your CRM.
  • Google Calendar busy check and calendar feed (Pro).

✅ Bookings, Contacts and Dashboard

  • All Events: meetings, webinars and booked appointments in one list, with search by client email, bulk actions, and a Needs attention tab for overlaps and missing links. Calendar view (Pro).
  • Book a client in: add a booking yourself; MeetingHub checks the time is free and emails the client.
  • Manage each booking: reschedule, cancel with a reason the client sees, mark completed or no-show, keep private notes, and join as host.
  • Contacts: everyone who booked you, with how often they came, their no-shows and their next booking. Notes, full history and export (Pro).
  • Dashboard: the last 30 days on one screen: events held, bookings, cancellation rate, hours on calls, what is live, what is next and what needs you. Any date range and revenue (Pro).
  • Export bookings: download every booking as a spreadsheet, answers included.
  • Site Health checks: your platform connections are tested, and a log of platform errors helps you fix them.

✅ Works With Your WordPress Site

  • Block editor, Elementor, Bricks and the Classic editor: blocks, widgets and shortcodes for booking and meetings.
  • WooCommerce and BricksMembers: members-only meetings for buyers and members.
  • Yoast SEO and Rank Math: booking pages in their sitemaps.
  • Multilingual: translation ready, and works beside Polylang and WPML.
  • Multisite: each site keeps its own bookings, meetings and accounts.
  • Privacy tools: bookings are part of WordPress personal data export and erasure.
  • For developers: filters such as mhub_user_can_access_meeting, and a meetinghub:booking browser event for your tracking tools.

🔥 Get MeetingHub PRO | 📖 Docs | 🤝 Join Community | 🕹️ YouTube

🎯 Use Cases

  • Consultants and coaches: paid or free sessions with the video link already in the confirmation.
  • Telehealth and online therapy: patients book a consultation and join from their email.
  • Tutors and online classes: office hours, lessons and course sessions.
  • Legal, tax and financial advisers: remote consultations, with client records on your own server.
  • Agencies and freelancers: a discovery call link for a proposal or an email signature.
  • Webinars and online events: Zoom webinars and meetings listed on any page.

📢 Hear From Our Users

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Great Plugin!

Functional and complete plugin, it allows you to integrate all the main video conferencing platforms. Technical assistance is available and responsive to any user problems, solving them very quickly. The Pugin is constantly updated to develop improvements and add new features, listening to the needs of users! Highly recommended.

by @giomax86

😍 Other Plugins from Our Team

  • DriveHub – Google Drive integration: embed files, photo galleries, file lists, uploads and downloads
  • GoodMeet – Meetings and classes for Google Meet
  • ZooMeet – Zoom meetings and webinars, with a join page for each
  • TogMeet – Schedule Microsoft Teams meetings from WordPress
  • WeMeet – Schedule Webex meetings from WordPress

External services

MeetingHub talks to the services below only after you connect one, create a meeting on it, or a visitor joins or books one. Freemius is used only if you opt in.

Bookings: a booking on a page set to Zoom, Google Meet, Microsoft Teams or Webex sends that service the start time, length, time zone and a meeting title (with the client’s name for one-to-one appointments), and later changes or cancellation. Client email, phone, notes and answers stay in your database.

Zoom (Zoom Communications, Inc.) creates, updates and deletes meetings and webinars once you connect Zoom, and reads the list of active users on your account so you can pick a meeting’s host. It receives your Server-to-Server credentials, meeting details (title, agenda, time, time zone, password, duration, options) and, with webinar registration, registrant name and email. “Join in Browser” loads the Zoom Meeting SDK and its React, Redux and lodash builds from source.zoom.us and sends Zoom the name and email the attendee enters. Terms, Privacy.

Google Meet / Google Calendar (Google LLC) creates and updates Meet events once you upload Google credentials. It receives the credentials, and the title, description, times, time zone, attendee emails and reminder and visibility settings of each event. “Add to Google Calendar” opens google.com with the title, time and link only when a visitor clicks it. Terms, Privacy.

Webex (Cisco Systems, Inc.) creates, updates and deletes meetings once you connect Webex. It receives your OAuth credentials, meeting details (title, agenda, password, times, time zone, options) and, with registration, registrant name and email. Terms, Privacy.

Microsoft Teams / Microsoft Graph (Microsoft Corporation) creates and updates Teams meetings once you connect Microsoft. It receives your app credentials (client ID, secret, tenant ID) and each meeting’s subject, times and length. Terms, Privacy.

Jitsi Meet hosts calls on the server you choose in MeetingHub → Integrations. The room name and the joining person’s display name go to that server.

  • Public server (default): one of these community servers, not run by us, each under its operator’s own terms. Set your own domain or JaaS to avoid them.
  • jitsi.member.fsf.org, Free Software Foundation: Privacy.
  • meet.evolix.org, Evolix: Terms and data protection, Legal notice and privacy.
  • video.devloprog.org, Devloprog: Terms of use.
  • webconf.viviers-fibre.net, Association Viviers Fibre (website): publishes no separate terms or privacy policy.
  • JaaS on 8x8.vc (8×8, Inc.): a moderator who can edit posts joins with a signed token holding their WordPress user ID, name, email and avatar URL. Terms, Privacy. The avatar comes from Gravatar (Automattic Inc.): Terms, Privacy.
  • Self-hosted: your own server, under its own terms.

Gravatar (Automattic Inc.) shows the host’s photo on booking pages when avatars are on (Settings → Discussion). The site checks once per host every 12 hours whether a photo exists for the hashed email; visitors’ browsers load it from Gravatar. Turn avatars off to stop both. Terms, Privacy.

Calendly (Calendly LLC), only when you use Import from Calendly: your access token goes to api.calendly.com to read your event types and schedule, and is never stored. Terms, Privacy.

Freemius (Freemius, Inc.) handles opt-in and account pages. Nothing is sent unless an administrator opts in after activation; “Skip” sends nothing. Opting in sends your name, email, site URL, WordPress, PHP and plugin versions and active plugins and themes. Deactivation feedback is sent only if you submit it. The Contact Us page loads a form from wp.freemius.com, and the Account page links to checkout.freemius.com. Terms, Privacy.
sections.installation:
1. Go to Plugins → Add New, search for MeetingHub, then click Install Now and Activate.
  2. Open Booking setup. Your first booking page is already there, with its link to copy.
  3. To make another, click New booking page, pick a starting point, and click Create booking page.
  4. Share the link, or paste [meetinghub_booking link="your-link"] into any page.

To install by hand, download the ZIP from WordPress.org, upload it on Plugins → Add New → Upload Plugin, activate it, and follow steps 2 to 4.

No account is needed to start. Jitsi Meet works at once, and Zoom, Google Meet, Microsoft Teams and Webex connect on Integrations → Video platforms when you want them.
sections.faq:
What is MeetingHub?

MeetingHub is a WordPress plugin for appointment booking and video meetings. Clients book a time on your site, and each booking gets a meeting link on Zoom, Google Meet, Microsoft Teams, Webex or Jitsi Meet. You can also create, list and embed meetings and Zoom webinars without any booking at all.

Is MeetingHub free?

Yes. Booking pages, availability, buffers, time zones, booking emails and reminders, contacts, the dashboard and all five video platforms are free, with no cap on pages, appointments or meetings. Features marked (Pro) in this readme need the paid add-on.

Is there a free booking plugin that creates Zoom links?

Yes. Set a MeetingHub booking page’s location to Zoom, connect your Zoom account once, and every appointment booked on it gets its own Zoom meeting, with the join link in both confirmation emails and the calendar file. Google Meet, Microsoft Teams, Webex and Jitsi Meet work the same way, all in the free plugin.

How do I add an appointment booking calendar to WordPress?

Install MeetingHub and open Booking setup. Your first booking page is ready, Monday to Friday, 9 to 5, with a video link included. Share its address, or paste [meetinghub_booking link="your-link"] into any page, or add the Booking page block. It takes about two minutes and needs no account connected.

How do people book a time with me?

They open your link and pick a day, then a free time, shown in their own time zone. They enter their name, email and a note, and confirm. You both get an email, the appointment carries a calendar file, and if the page uses a video platform the meeting link is created and included.

Do I need a Zoom or Google account to take bookings?

No. Choose Phone call or In person and no video account is involved. Choose Jitsi Meet and the meeting room is made without an account. Connecting Zoom, Google Meet, Microsoft Teams or Webex is a separate step you can take later.

Do I pay extra for Zoom, Google Meet or Teams?

No. Many booking plugins sell each video integration as a paid extra. MeetingHub includes Zoom, Google Meet, Microsoft Teams, Webex and Jitsi Meet in the free plugin, and never charges for meeting minutes. Any time limit on a call is your own plan’s on that service.

Is MeetingHub a Calendly alternative?

It does the same job on your own WordPress site. Your booking pages sit on your domain under your theme, client data stays in your database, and there is no monthly charge per person and no commission. In exchange, updates and backups are yours to run, where a hosted service does them for you.

Can I move my booking links from Calendly?

Yes. On Booking setup, press Import from Calendly and paste a personal access token from Calendly (Integrations, then API and webhooks). Each event type you pick becomes a booking page with the same name, length, description and place, and keeps its link name, so calendly.com/you/intro becomes yoursite.com/booking/intro/. The token is used for the import only and never stored.

Can MeetingHub stop double bookings?

Yes. The slot is claimed in the database with a uniqueness check, not in the browser, so two people clicking the same time in the same second cannot both get it. The second one is told the time has gone and sees what is still free.

Can I set buffers, minimum notice and how far ahead people can book?

Yes, all three, free and set per page. A buffer adds a gap before or after each appointment. Minimum notice stops a booking for twenty minutes from now. The booking window caps how far into the future your calendar goes.

Does MeetingHub send appointment reminders?

Yes. The free plugin sends one reminder email before each appointment, at a lead time you choose from one hour to one week. Confirmation, reschedule and cancellation emails go to both sides automatically. More reminders and text messages are (Pro).

Does it sync with Google Calendar, Outlook or Apple Calendar?

Every confirmation and reschedule email carries a calendar file, so the appointment lands in Google Calendar, Outlook, Apple Calendar or any calendar app. Checking your Google Calendar for busy times and a live calendar feed are (Pro).

Can clients change or cancel their own appointment?

Yes. Every confirmation carries a private link to move to another free time or cancel, with a reason if they want to give one. You are told either way, and the new calendar file is sent automatically.

Does MeetingHub handle time zones?

Yes. You set your hours in your own time zone once. Each visitor sees times on their own clock, detected from the browser, and can pick another zone when booking for someone else. The stored appointment is the same moment for both of you.

Can I put the booking form inside my own page or page builder?

Yes. Use the Booking page block in the block editor, the shortcode [meetinghub_booking link="your-link"] in Elementor, Bricks or the Classic editor, or a popup: give any link the class mhub-book-popup. The form takes your theme’s column width.

Can I take payments for appointments?

Card payments are (Pro). Clients pay by card, Apple Pay or Google Pay on Stripe before the booking is confirmed, and you can take deposits, sell extras, add tax and tips, sell session packages and refund in one click. Free booking pages take bookings without payment.

Can several team members share one booking page?

Team booking pages are (Pro): round robin, where the booking goes to whoever is free, or all hosts together on one call. Hosts who are not administrators get their own pages, hours and bookings and nothing else.

Who is MeetingHub for?

Anyone whose appointments happen online or by phone: consultants, coaches and therapists, telehealth practitioners, tutors and course creators, legal and financial advisers, agencies and freelancers. It is not made for salons, hotels, rentals or restaurant tables, where a plugin for in-person resources will suit you better.

Can I use MeetingHub for telehealth?

Yes. Patients book a consultation and join from their confirmation email. MeetingHub alone does not make a site HIPAA compliant: bookings are stored in your WordPress database and calls run on the video service you pick, so compliance depends on your hosting and on the agreement you have with that service.

Which video platforms can I connect?

Five: Zoom, Google Meet, Microsoft Teams, Webex and Jitsi Meet. All five are free, and one site can use as many as it needs.

Where does the meeting actually happen?

On the service you picked. MeetingHub creates the meeting through that service’s API and links or embeds it on your site, so video, audio and recording are handled by Zoom, Google, Microsoft, Cisco or Jitsi. Your hosting is never in the path of the call.

How do I put a meeting on a page?

Use the MeetingHub Event block, the Elementor widget or a shortcode such as [mhub-zoom-meeting id="123"]. List shortcodes such as [mhub-zoom-meeting-list category="coaching-101"] show many meetings, filtered by meeting category.

Can I make a meeting members-only?

Yes, free. Limit a meeting to people who bought a WooCommerce product or to BricksMembers members, and limit a meeting list to chosen roles or users. Visitors who may not join see a private event card with a log in button.

Can I brand my booking page?

Yes. The Classic theme comes in Light and Dark, and every new page is previewed before you publish it. 18 more themes, any colour, a theme per page and Match my brand are (Pro).

Can I record a meeting?

Yes, on the service you connected. Zoom and Webex auto recording are free settings. The recording is made and kept by that service.

Do booking pages work with Yoast SEO and Rank Math?

Yes. Each booking page can have its own search title, description and share image, and pages you show in search are added to your sitemap, including the sitemaps of Yoast SEO and Rank Math. Pages stay out of search until you switch it on.

Can AI assistants book appointments on my site?

Yes, on WordPress 6.9 or later. An AI assistant connected to your site through the WordPress Abilities API can list your booking pages, find free times and book one, following every rule the page has.

Is MeetingHub translation ready?

Yes. Every screen and email is translatable. Add ?lang= and a language code to a booking link to open it in that language; with Polylang or WPML the parameter is ?mhub_lang=. Booking emails are written in your site’s language.

Where is my client data stored, and can I export or delete it?

In your own WordPress database. Nothing about an appointment is sent to us. Bookings are part of WordPress’s personal data tools, so Tools → Export Personal Data returns everything held for an email address and Tools → Erase Personal Data anonymises it, which is what a GDPR or CCPA request needs.

Which PHP versions does it support?

PHP 7.4 up to 8.3. Google Meet needs PHP 8.1 or later, because Google’s own libraries do; on older PHP it says so, and everything else works as usual.

Does it work on WordPress Multisite?

Yes. Each site in the network keeps its own booking pages, bookings, meetings and connected accounts.

Does the admin interface load on the front of my site?

Not for your visitors. The admin application loads only for signed-in users who are allowed to create meetings. Somebody reading a page while logged out never receives it.

What happens if I disconnect an account?

Meetings already created on that service keep their links, because they live on the service. MeetingHub stops creating new ones there until you reconnect. Nothing is deleted at either end.

What is removed when I delete the plugin?

Deleting MeetingHub from the Plugins screen removes its settings, connected credentials and cached data. Your meetings and booked appointments are kept, so reinstalling never loses a commitment to a client. Delete bookings first if you want them gone too.

Is MeetingHub affiliated with Zoom, Google, Microsoft or Cisco?

No. MeetingHub is made by Sovlix and connects to these services through their public APIs. Zoom is a trademark of Zoom Communications, Google Meet of Google LLC, Microsoft Teams of Microsoft Corporation, Webex of Cisco Systems, and Jitsi of 8×8, Inc.

Where is the source code of the compiled files?

The compiled files in assets/dist/ are built from assets/src/ (JavaScript and SCSS), which ships in this plugin. package.json lists the build tools: run npm install, then NODE_ENV=production npm run build and NODE_ENV=production npm run build:getstarted. The webpack, Tailwind and PostCSS configuration files are kept in the development repository. PHP libraries: composer install --no-dev.

Bundled open-source libraries, all GPL-compatible: Jitsi Meet External API (Apache-2.0); Google API Client, Google Auth, Guzzle, Monolog, firebase/php-jwt and their dependencies in vendor/ (Apache-2.0, MIT, BSD-3-Clause); Freemius SDK (GPL-3.0); React, React Router, moment-timezone, axios, crypto-js, react-select, react-datepicker, react-datetime, react-time-picker, react-toastify, react-tooltip, react-simple-wysiwyg and @wordpress packages compiled into assets/dist/ (MIT, GPL-2.0+). The Zoom Meeting SDK is not bundled; Zoom serves it on browser join.

Where can I get help?

Read the guides at sovlix.com/docs, ask on the WordPress.org support forum, or join the Sovlix community.

short_description: Free appointment booking and scheduling. Every booking gets its own Zoom, Google Meet, Teams, Webex or Jitsi link. Run video meetings too.
description:
MeetingHub is a free appointment booking and scheduling plugin for WordPress that gives every booking its own Zoom, Google Meet, Microsoft Teams, Webex or Jitsi meeting link.

Share a booking page, and clients pick a time from your real availability, on their own clock. The booking is confirmed at once, both of you get an email with a calendar file, and the join link is already in it.

Many booking plugins sell video conferencing as a paid extra. MeetingHub includes all five video platforms in the free plugin, with no cap on booking pages, appointments or meetings, no commission, and every client record kept in your own WordPress database. The same plugin also creates and lists your Zoom meetings and webinars, Google Meet, Teams, Webex and Jitsi meetings.

🔥 Get MeetingHub PRO | 📖 Docs | 🤝 Join Community | 🕹️ YouTube

🏆 Why MeetingHub

  • Video on every booking, free: Zoom, Google Meet, Microsoft Teams, Webex and Jitsi Meet are all in the free plugin, and each page picks its own.
  • Works before you connect anything: Jitsi Meet needs no account, so your first booking can have a working meeting link in two minutes.
  • No limits, no commission: unlimited booking pages, appointments and meetings, with nothing taken from what you charge.
  • Your clients stay yours: names, emails and bookings live in your WordPress database, ready to export or erase.
  • Made for WordPress: blocks, Elementor, shortcodes, Yoast SEO and Rank Math sitemaps, multisite and translations.

✅ Appointment Booking Calendar

Set your hours once, share a link, and people book the times you have free.

  • A booking page for every service: each one has its own address, such as /booking/consultation/, with a month view and the free times of the chosen day.
  • Your booking calendar anywhere: paste [meetinghub_booking link="your-link"], add the Booking page block, or open it in a popup from any button or menu link.
  • Weekly hours and days off: working hours per day, days off, and different hours on a single date. New pages follow your site defaults.
  • Buffers, notice and booking window: gaps around each appointment, a minimum notice, how far ahead people may book, and how often start times appear.
  • Time zones handled: visitors see every time on their own clock and can switch zones. Your hours stay on yours.
  • No double bookings: each slot is claimed in the database, so two people clicking the same time cannot both get it.
  • Video, phone, in person or your own link: every page picks one way to meet.
  • A short booking form: name, email, a phone field with the country code, and notes. Custom questions (Pro).
  • Clients reschedule or cancel themselves: every confirmation carries a private link, and a client can say why they cancel.
  • Your own thank-you message: tell clients what happens next the moment they book.
  • Hidden booking pages: bookable by their link, left out of every list.
  • Ready from the start: your first booking page is made for you, and new ones start from a use case such as Consultation, Discovery call or Tutoring session.
  • Import from Calendly: bring your event types over as booking pages, with their link names and your working hours.
  • Bookable by AI assistants: on WordPress 6.9 or later, an AI assistant connected to your site can find your free times and book them.
  • Team booking pages (Pro): round robin or all hosts together, and hosts who are not administrators.
  • Routing forms (Pro): ask a question or two, then send each visitor to the right page.
  • Group and recurring bookings (Pro): several places per time, and the same slot every week or two.
  • Approval, limits and holidays (Pro): confirm each booking yourself, cap bookings a day or a week, save schedules, and close every calendar for a holiday.
  • Protected booking pages (Pro): a password, single-use links, or work email only.

✅ Payments for Appointments (Pro)

  • Card payments (Pro): clients pay by card, Apple Pay or Google Pay on Stripe before the booking is confirmed, with refunds in one click.
  • Deposits, extras, tax and tips (Pro): charge part up front, sell add-ons at checkout, and add a tax line or a tip.
  • Session packages (Pro): sell 5 or 10 sessions at once, booked later with a code.

✅ Video Meetings on Zoom, Google Meet, Teams, Webex and Jitsi

Each meeting and each booking page picks its own platform, so one site can run all five.

  • Zoom: meetings and webinars, host and alternative hosts, auto recording, and Join in browser so guests need no Zoom app.
  • Google Meet: every meeting is a real Google Calendar event, with its attendees and time zone.
  • Microsoft Teams: meetings over a secure Microsoft Graph connection, with lobby settings.
  • Webex: meetings with breakout sessions, meeting lock, auto recording and join before host.
  • Jitsi Meet: no account needed, on a public server, your own domain or 8×8 JaaS.
  • Meeting setup: defaults for every platform on one screen, with a preview of what guests see, and a step-by-step connection guide for each.
  • Meeting pages: a countdown, a Join button, and your choice of header, footer and sidebar. More themes, layouts, an agenda and Add to calendar (Pro).
  • Show meetings anywhere: the MeetingHub Event block and Elementor widget show a meeting as a card, a compact card or its full page.
  • Members-only meetings: limit a meeting to buyers of a WooCommerce product or BricksMembers members, and a meeting list to chosen roles or users.
  • My Meetings: [mhub-my-meetings] shows a signed-in member their upcoming sessions and bookings, each with a Join button.
  • Registration, recurring meetings, recordings and reports (Pro): on the platforms that support them.
  • Front-end meetings (Pro): members create and manage their own meetings from the front of your site.
  • Courses and marketplaces (Pro): Tutor LMS, LearnPress, LifterLMS and Academy LMS courses; Dokan, WCFM and MultiVendorX vendors; meetings sold with WooCommerce.

✅ Booking Page Themes, SEO and Languages

  • Classic theme in Light and Dark: set once for every booking page on Booking setup → Page design, previewed on your own page.
  • 18 designer themes (Pro): Summit, Sage, Calm and more, plus the Waves, Aura and Botanica styles, in any colour, with a theme per page and Match my brand.
  • Search and sharing: give each booking page its own search title, description and share image. Pages you show in search join your sitemap, including Yoast SEO and Rank Math.
  • In your visitor’s language: add ?lang= and a language code to a page link to open it in that language.
  • QR code for every page (Pro).

✅ Booking Emails, Reminders and Calendar Files

  • Eight booking emails: confirmation, reminder, rescheduled and cancelled for the client; new, moved, cancelled and no meeting link for you. Each one can be edited, previewed, tested or switched off.
  • Appointment reminder email: one before each appointment, from one hour to one week ahead.
  • Calendar file on every confirmation: an .ics attachment that adds the appointment to Google Calendar, Outlook or Apple Calendar.
  • Know your emails arrived: a log of every booking email, failures first, with a Send again button.
  • Text messages (Pro): confirmations and reminders from your own Twilio number.
  • More emails and automations (Pro): follow-ups, no-show notes, extra reminders and webhooks to Zapier, Make or your CRM.
  • Google Calendar busy check and calendar feed (Pro).

✅ Bookings, Contacts and Dashboard

  • All Events: meetings, webinars and booked appointments in one list, with search by client email, bulk actions, and a Needs attention tab for overlaps and missing links. Calendar view (Pro).
  • Book a client in: add a booking yourself; MeetingHub checks the time is free and emails the client.
  • Manage each booking: reschedule, cancel with a reason the client sees, mark completed or no-show, keep private notes, and join as host.
  • Contacts: everyone who booked you, with how often they came, their no-shows and their next booking. Notes, full history and export (Pro).
  • Dashboard: the last 30 days on one screen: events held, bookings, cancellation rate, hours on calls, what is live, what is next and what needs you. Any date range and revenue (Pro).
  • Export bookings: download every booking as a spreadsheet, answers included.
  • Site Health checks: your platform connections are tested, and a log of platform errors helps you fix them.

✅ Works With Your WordPress Site

  • Block editor, Elementor, Bricks and the Classic editor: blocks, widgets and shortcodes for booking and meetings.
  • WooCommerce and BricksMembers: members-only meetings for buyers and members.
  • Yoast SEO and Rank Math: booking pages in their sitemaps.
  • Multilingual: translation ready, and works beside Polylang and WPML.
  • Multisite: each site keeps its own bookings, meetings and accounts.
  • Privacy tools: bookings are part of WordPress personal data export and erasure.
  • For developers: filters such as mhub_user_can_access_meeting, and a meetinghub:booking browser event for your tracking tools.

🔥 Get MeetingHub PRO | 📖 Docs | 🤝 Join Community | 🕹️ YouTube

🎯 Use Cases

  • Consultants and coaches: paid or free sessions with the video link already in the confirmation.
  • Telehealth and online therapy: patients book a consultation and join from their email.
  • Tutors and online classes: office hours, lessons and course sessions.
  • Legal, tax and financial advisers: remote consultations, with client records on your own server.
  • Agencies and freelancers: a discovery call link for a proposal or an email signature.
  • Webinars and online events: Zoom webinars and meetings listed on any page.

📢 Hear From Our Users

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Great Plugin!

Functional and complete plugin, it allows you to integrate all the main video conferencing platforms. Technical assistance is available and responsive to any user problems, solving them very quickly. The Pugin is constantly updated to develop improvements and add new features, listening to the needs of users! Highly recommended.

by @giomax86

😍 Other Plugins from Our Team

  • DriveHub – Google Drive integration: embed files, photo galleries, file lists, uploads and downloads
  • GoodMeet – Meetings and classes for Google Meet
  • ZooMeet – Zoom meetings and webinars, with a join page for each
  • TogMeet – Schedule Microsoft Teams meetings from WordPress
  • WeMeet – Schedule Webex meetings from WordPress

External services

MeetingHub talks to the services below only after you connect one, create a meeting on it, or a visitor joins or books one. Freemius is used only if you opt in.

Bookings: a booking on a page set to Zoom, Google Meet, Microsoft Teams or Webex sends that service the start time, length, time zone and a meeting title (with the client’s name for one-to-one appointments), and later changes or cancellation. Client email, phone, notes and answers stay in your database.

Zoom (Zoom Communications, Inc.) creates, updates and deletes meetings and webinars once you connect Zoom, and reads the list of active users on your account so you can pick a meeting’s host. It receives your Server-to-Server credentials, meeting details (title, agenda, time, time zone, password, duration, options) and, with webinar registration, registrant name and email. “Join in Browser” loads the Zoom Meeting SDK and its React, Redux and lodash builds from source.zoom.us and sends Zoom the name and email the attendee enters. Terms, Privacy.

Google Meet / Google Calendar (Google LLC) creates and updates Meet events once you upload Google credentials. It receives the credentials, and the title, description, times, time zone, attendee emails and reminder and visibility settings of each event. “Add to Google Calendar” opens google.com with the title, time and link only when a visitor clicks it. Terms, Privacy.

Webex (Cisco Systems, Inc.) creates, updates and deletes meetings once you connect Webex. It receives your OAuth credentials, meeting details (title, agenda, password, times, time zone, options) and, with registration, registrant name and email. Terms, Privacy.

Microsoft Teams / Microsoft Graph (Microsoft Corporation) creates and updates Teams meetings once you connect Microsoft. It receives your app credentials (client ID, secret, tenant ID) and each meeting’s subject, times and length. Terms, Privacy.

Jitsi Meet hosts calls on the server you choose in MeetingHub → Integrations. The room name and the joining person’s display name go to that server.

  • Public server (default): one of these community servers, not run by us, each under its operator’s own terms. Set your own domain or JaaS to avoid them.
  • jitsi.member.fsf.org, Free Software Foundation: Privacy.
  • meet.evolix.org, Evolix: Terms and data protection, Legal notice and privacy.
  • video.devloprog.org, Devloprog: Terms of use.
  • webconf.viviers-fibre.net, Association Viviers Fibre (website): publishes no separate terms or privacy policy.
  • JaaS on 8x8.vc (8×8, Inc.): a moderator who can edit posts joins with a signed token holding their WordPress user ID, name, email and avatar URL. Terms, Privacy. The avatar comes from Gravatar (Automattic Inc.): Terms, Privacy.
  • Self-hosted: your own server, under its own terms.

Gravatar (Automattic Inc.) shows the host’s photo on booking pages when avatars are on (Settings → Discussion). The site checks once per host every 12 hours whether a photo exists for the hashed email; visitors’ browsers load it from Gravatar. Turn avatars off to stop both. Terms, Privacy.

Calendly (Calendly LLC), only when you use Import from Calendly: your access token goes to api.calendly.com to read your event types and schedule, and is never stored. Terms, Privacy.

Freemius (Freemius, Inc.) handles opt-in and account pages. Nothing is sent unless an administrator opts in after activation; “Skip” sends nothing. Opting in sends your name, email, site URL, WordPress, PHP and plugin versions and active plugins and themes. Deactivation feedback is sent only if you submit it. The Contact Us page loads a form from wp.freemius.com, and the Account page links to checkout.freemius.com. Terms, Privacy.
